title: El curso que paga la empresa
label: ch:es-pago
canDo: I can follow a conversation about who pays for something: hear that an amount is deducted over months rather than taken all at once, and match that to a statement saying the opposite in different words.

payoff.summary: Match a statement about paying the full amount at once against a speaker who says the opposite in different words.
payoff.note: THE LAST AUTHORABLE A2 VOCABULARY CHAPTER. After this one, every remaining lexeme in the A2 gap is ALREADY TAUGHT and blocked only by how the audit measures: creer, explicar and problema (HL-C418, HL-C420) and responder (HL-C422). Teaching any of them again is the duplication HL-C418 forbids, so the vocabulary pipeline stops here until those decisions are made. IT CLEARS NO ITEM, for the third chapter running. Item 3's row also needs explicar; item 43's also needs creer. Expect 4 words, 2 lexemes off the list, 0 items. THE HL-C421 CHECK FOUND TWO MORE, ITS FIFTH CONSECUTIVE HIT. Item 43 is a MATCHING task, so the STATEMENT is the text to read rather than an option set: "Pensaba que habia que pagar el IMPORTE completo de una vez", against a passage reading "te lo descuentan en doce meses, no DE GOLPE". Neither `importe` nor `golpe` is in the requires row and both had zero hits corpus-wide -- importe's three greps were the English word `imported` inside ES-C367-desayuno and ES-C393-nacionalidad. `de golpe` is load-bearing: it is what the statement's `de una vez` has to be matched against, so without it the item is closed even to a reader who understood every sentence. The synthesis teaches exactly that pairing and names the general rule -- a matching task rewards PARAPHRASE, so the words worth learning are the ones that come in pairs. Fourteen other words across the two items were verified taught (companero, todavia, simpatico, serio, amable, funcionar, ayudar, traer, poco, pagar, entero, completo, principio, contar). THREE OF THE FOUR CAME OUT OF WORDS THE BOOK ALREADY HELD, so most of the chapter is hand-over rather than introduction. ES-C282-invitado already names invitar outright ("from invitar, Latin invitare, to invite; invitado is its participle"), the same move used for lectura, avisar and llamada. ES-C463-importar teaches importar as `to matter` AND notes the literal import sense, so el importe is its THIRD job and the lesson presents all three together, joined by in- plus portare, to carry in: goods carried in are imports, a thing that carries weight matters, and what a bill carries in for you to pay is its importe. descontar is contar with des-. THE des- NUANCE IS ALREADY OWNED AND IS CITED RATHER THAN RESTATED. ES-C315-descanso owns des- as an undoing, and ES-C444-cubrir owns the harder half: "Compare disfrutar, where the prefix did not reverse at all. Same shape, two behaviours, and only the meaning of the whole word tells you which you have." So descontar cites cubrir's table and places itself in the reversing camp explicitly -- contar adds up, descontar takes away from the total. COUSIN LINKS: importe takes importare-latin, already held by ES-C398-importante AND ES-C463-importar, so the three are cousins by the join key; descontar takes computare-latin from ES-C38-contar. Only invitare-latin and colaphus-latin are newly minted -- ES-C282-invitado carries roots: [] so invitar had no slug to inherit. The portare family already in the corpus (deporte, polideportivo, comportamiento) is named in the importe lesson so the learner sees the group. GOLPE'S ETYMOLOGY IS THE ONE OUTSIDER and earns its place: Latin colaphus from Greek kolaphos, a box on the ear, worn down by losing its middle syllable and softening c to g, which is why it no longer looks Greek. English kept the same blow intact in coup, so golpe de estado and coup d'etat are the same two words said twice -- and estado was taught in chapter 473, one chapter earlier. CAUGHT IN MY OWN DRAFT BY THE TOKEN SWEEP, FOURTH CONSECUTIVE CHAPTER: `el importe de la matricula` used matricula, which has zero corpus hits. Replaced with `el importe del curso`, curso being taught at ES-C417-curso. The first replacement then tripped the standalone-book check on the phrase `the course`, the same rule chapter 471 hit, and the gloss was reworded to `the fee for a class`.
